comment: Each entry in props must contain an object with exactly one key-value pair,
where the key is the name of the variable to set in the global scope, and the value is the value to assign to that variable.
Values can reference previously defined variables using the $() syntax, and those references will be expanded when the variable is set.
Note that the script only reads the props array, and the variable-descriptions are for documentation purposes only and are not used by the script.

variable-descriptions.targetRoot: The root directory for the CDL2 release.
variable-descriptions.sampleDBName: The name of the sample database file.
variable-descriptions.sampleDBLocation: The full path to the sample database file, constructed from targetRoot and sampleDBName.
variable-descriptions.WSLDistro: The name of the WSL distribution to use.
variable-descriptions.WSLDir: The directory within the WSL distribution where the lab files are located.
variable-descriptions.WSLDistroDir: The full path to the WSL distribution directory, constructed from WSLDistro.
variable-descriptions.WSLTarget: The full path to the target directory within WSL, constructed from WSLDistroDir and WSLDir.
variable-descriptions.WindowsTarget: The target directory on Windows where files will be copied. NOTE: This directory will contain targetRoot, everything is under there.
variable-descriptions.releaseDir: The directory where the CDL2 release will be built.
variable-descriptions.source: The source directory containing the CDL2 project files.
variable-descriptions.VSProjectDir: The directory containing the Visual Studio project files for CDL2, constructed from source.
variable-descriptions.targetDir: The directory where the final release files are constructed, used to deploy to GitHub.
